evidence: Abstract: 'MAST-Data ... 1600+ annotated traces'; 'We develop MAST through rigorous analysis of 150 traces ... identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.'
correction: MAST: 14 failure modes in 3 categories (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification), derived from 150 expert-annotated traces (kappa=0.88); MAST-Data has 1600+ traces across 7 MAS frameworks. No top-level tool-fault category (our reading of the taxonomy, not a statement in the paper). Authors: Cemri, Pan, Yang, ..., Zaharia, Gonzalez, Stoica.

evidence: Abstract: 'cascading failures, where a single root-cause error propagates through subsequent decisions'; 'AgentErrorTaxonomy, a modular classification of failure modes spanning memory, reflection, planning, action, and system-level operations.'
correction: Exact title: 'Where LLM Agents Fail and How They can Learn From Failures' (Zhu et al., arXiv:2509.25370, 2025).

evidence: Abstract: 'The best method achieves 53.5% accuracy in identifying failure-responsible agents but only 14.2% in pinpointing failure steps, with some methods performing below random.'
correction: Full title: 'Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems' (Zhang et al., 2025; Who&When dataset, 127 MAS).

evidence: Abstract: 'We also propose a new metric (pass^k) ... even state-of-the-art function calling agents (like gpt-4o) succeed on <50% of the tasks, and are quite inconsistent (pass^8 <25% in retail).'
correction: Full title: 'tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains' (Yao, Shinn, Razavi, Narasimhan, 2024).

evidence: MSR abstract: 'key feature of gray failure is differential observability: that the system's failure detectors may not notice problems even when applications are afflicted by them.'
correction: Venue: HotOS 2017 (ACM). Authors: Peng (Ryan) Huang, Chuanxiong Guo, Lidong Zhou, Jacob R. Lorch, Yingnong Dang, Murali Chintalapati, Randolph Yao.

evidence: Abstract: 'the majority of catastrophic failures could easily have been prevented by performing simple testing on error handling code – the last line of defense'
correction: Full title adds ': An Analysis of Production Failures in Distributed Data-Intensive Systems' (OSDI '14, pp. 249-265; 198 user-reported failures).

evidence: Abstract p.1: 'empirical study on the descriptions of 3 075 Web APIs ... only 517 APIs consistently release major upgrades ... while 1 970 APIs will not always correctly inform their clients about breaking changes'
correction: Authors: Souhaila Serbout, Cesare Pautasso (USI); ICWE 2024. Note: 'in the best case' qualifier; analysis is OpenAPI-description diffs, so behavioral changes are not counted.

evidence: Abstract: 'Inline text was sufficient for false-code adoption in 60/60 trials; the tool-result condition produced 57/60 ... did not find greater behavioral weight for the result package than for announced inline text.'
correction: Single author Justin Bronder; single model (Claude Opus 5), one synthetic task template, one API. Exploratory study did find tool-result > assistant-assertion (14/24 vs 0/22; replication 7/24 vs 0/24).
